# Sizes, in BYTES, of the self-host driver binaries CI already builds, plus
# the compiler's own output for itself — checked against every run by
# scripts/ci-check-driver-sizes (#6826).
#
# WHICH BINARY IS "THE SELF-HOST BINARY": fern.fern/stage2, named below as the
# tracked artifact. It is compiler/fern.fern, the whole self-hosted
# compiler CLI, COMPILED BY ITSELF (the fern.fern driver, built by the pin,
# compiling its own source — the bootstrap chain's stage2), so it is the one
# row that moves with the current compiler's code generation, and it is the
# number to quote when talking about self-host binary size (#4109's "well
# under half" target is against it). Every other row is a driver built by the
# PINNED stage0 compiler (bootstrap/stage0.lock): those rows move with the
# drivers' sources and the stdlib, never with a codegen change in the current
# compiler, and a pin refresh moves them all. `fern.fern` is the pin's build
# of the CLI (stage1); `asm_ir_run` is the front-end plus the x86-64 IR
# backend, `wasm_ir_run` the front-end plus the wasm one, and so on. They are
# recorded because they are free to record and they localise a regression to
# a backend — NOT because they are interchangeable. Quoting one against
# another is how #4109 acquired a bogus "the epic is 4x off": a 245 MB CLI
# figure compared with a 59 MB wasm_ir_run figure.
#
# tracked-artifact: fern.fern/stage2
#
# HOW THIS IS MEASURED. The `driver-sizes` job of test-e2e-selfhost.yml reads
# the driver names out of this file, builds every one of them
# (TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver; fern.fern/stage2 is the warmed fern.fern run
# over its own source), stats each into FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT, and compares
# that report against this file. Both compilers' output is deterministic per
# input, so a given commit yields the same byte count on any runner — a
# difference here is a real change in the sources, the stdlib, the pin or
# (for fern.fern/stage2) the current compiler's codegen, not runner noise. A
# pin refresh re-baselines every pin-built row, in the same PR.
#
# ENFORCED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Drift past FERN_SIZE_TOLERANCE_PERCENT (5% by
# default) is a job-summary line, a warning annotation and a FAILED
# `driver-sizes` job. A SHRINK is flagged too: an un-updated baseline after a
# win silently raises the ceiling the next regression is measured against,
# which is how 16% of growth went unnoticed for eight days — and, in the other
# direction, how a 3.0 MB win was never recorded either (#7519).
#
# A DRIVER THAT WENT UNMEASURED FAILS TOO. `driver-sizes` sets
# FERN_SIZE_REPORT_COMPLETE=1, so a name in this file that reached no report is
# a finding instead of a row nobody notices is absent. The job used to union
# four per-job slices, each of which checked only the drivers it linked, so a
# five-row table ending in "every driver is within 5% of its baseline" was
# indistinguishable from a fifteen-row one — which is how the drivers grew 2.3x
# with the gate green.
#
# WHEN A NUMBER MOVES ON PURPOSE, update it in the same PR — the job summary
# prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not
# here; this file is a set of current facts.

# x86-64. The `driver-sizes` job is x86-only (the aarch64 lane skips the x86
# driver builds), so there is one architecture to baseline and no per-arch split.

# PICK THE DENOMINATOR THAT SEES YOUR CHANGE. A change confined to one module is
# honestly measured against the SMALLEST driver linking it, not against the
# tracked artifact: checker.fern -> checker_modload_run (3.7 MB), the front end
# or ssa -> ssa_run (3.1 MB), irlower.fern -> asm_ir_elig_run (12.0 MB).
# Dividing by the wrong one is not a small error. #7519 found the 311-loop
# checker migration registering EXACTLY 0 bytes against irlower_run, which does
# not link checker.fern at all, and found one irlower slice reading +6.8% or
# +9.2% for the same absolute growth depending only on which driver divided it.
